summary.steel_scope_overview: The BOQ defines a multi-phase CSA project with extensive structural steel and associated works. Major steel scopes include: primary structural steel frames for FSA and DCH buildings across four phases; steel roof decking for FSA/DCH and SSA buildings; large cooling tower gantry steelwork and associated access steel (stairs, ladders, railings, gratings) over MYD; structural steel supports across generator and USS trenches; numerous holding down bolt assemblies (H.D.A.) and grouting of steel bases; secondary steel for cladding and canopies; miscellaneous external steel such as bollards, crash protection, cat ladders and roof access stairs; and structural steel for standalone SSA buildings (Load Bank Garage, Fuel Polishing Building).
interfaces_and_risks: Heavy reliance on accurate casting and placement of H.D.A. and chemical anchors in concrete foundations for all steel works (frames, gantries, stairs). Errors here are a major risk to steel erection and alignment.

Multiple phases (PH1–PH4) act on the same structural zones (DCH, MYD, cooling tower gantry), so coordination of connection design, allowances for future phase loads, and detailing for continuity is critical.

Intumescent fire protection and corrosion protection (including galvanizing) must be compatible with steel grades and erection sequencing; misalignment of coatings with environment class (C2/C4) could cause rework.

Secondary steel for cladding, canopies and penetrations (cat ladders, canopies, AOVs, louvres) must align with primary steel and envelope details; late changes in envelope layout can impact steel secondary framing.
Trench steels (generator and USS) interface tightly with M&E equipment; mis-coordination of loads or support positions can affect serviceability and safety.
Extensive rooftop and gantry access steel (stairs, ladders, walkways) must comply with EN ISO 14122 and local code loading; misclassification can require reinforcement or replacement.
summary.concrete_items_handling: Concrete and purely civil items have been ignored except where they directly host, anchor or interface with steel (H.D.A., baseplates, hold-down assemblies, earthing at steel bases). All descriptions focusing solely on concrete properties, volume, mix, reinforcement and generic joints were excluded as out of metallic scope.
summary.extraction_notes: Project structure has been derived from BOQ package codes (e.g., S03-A2000, S05-A2000, S02-A7100, S02-A7200), descriptive headings (e.g., 'FSA - Structural Steel', 'DCH - Structural Steel', 'Cooling Tower Gantry'), and phase tags (PH1–PH4). Only items with direct structural steel relevance (primary frames, steel decking, fire and corrosion protection, access steel, secondary steel, holding down bolts, base grouting, earthing at steel, safety fabrications supporting stairs) have been retained as per the specified rules.
